```markdown
- Member: Rowan Delgado

- Reference number: POC-9391F374E1-41425
- Date of denial notice: August 18, 2026
- Service denied: Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
- Governing policy: **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02** (effective 2024-07-01), https://www.bcbsnd.com/providers/policies-precertification/legacy-medical-policy/c/cervical-fusions

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by my surgeon. The notice dated August 18, 2026 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records already submitted match the plan's own published criteria point for point. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this surgery is needed.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

The plan's policy, **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02**, sets out when this surgery is covered for degenerative disease:

> "ACDF) is considered medically necessary for treatment of symptomatic degenerative disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

**1. Unremitting symptoms with deficit, refractory to at least six weeks of conservative care.** The policy states:

> "unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit that are refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion:"

My records establish this:

- I have had **14 months of progressive neck pain that is not relieved by rest**.
- I have **radicular pain and numbness into my right thumb and index finger, with weakness**.
- My exam shows **positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level**.
- I completed **supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training — 8 weeks, from May 18, 2026 to July 13, 2026, 18 visits**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is longer than the six weeks the policy requires.
- I took **NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief**, and had a **corticosteroid injection on May 8, 2026 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief**.

**2. Imaging findings at the level being fused.** The policy lists the qualifying findings:

> " Herniated nucleus pulposus  Spondylosis (i.e., presence of osteophytes)  Visible loss of disc height compared to adjacent levels with resultant foraminal stenosis physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion"

My **MRI of the cervical spine dated June 26, 2026** shows a **C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression**. A herniated disc is the first finding on the plan's own list. Only one of the listed findings is required, and my imaging shows it at the single level proposed for fusion.

**3. Correlation between exam and imaging.** The policy requires that physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion. They do: the MRI shows **C6 nerve root compression on the right**, and my symptoms and exam findings are **on the right, in the thumb and index finger — the C6 distribution — with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level**.

I would also note that my records show **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker**.

## Request for the criteria that were actually applied

The denial notice tells me the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not tell me which criterion I failed to meet or how. I am asking the plan to send me, in writing, the specific criteria it applied to this request, the specific criterion it found unmet, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. The plan holds those criteria; I do not. I understand that BCBSND writes and publishes its own criteria free of charge and without a login, though the Medical Policy Search page runs on JavaScript, so a direct link often fails and the policy must be found by searching the CPT code. If the reviewer relied on anything beyond **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02**, I ask that it be identified and provided to me.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota overturn the denial dated August 18, 2026 (reference POC-9391F374E1-41425) and authorize CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Marchetti. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the exact criterion in **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02** that my records do not meet, and information on my next level of appeal, including external review.

This appeal must be received by **February 14, 2027**, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; any member who is unsure where to file can call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Please contact me at the phone number or address above if anything further is needed. I am happy to have additional records sent from Dr. Marchetti's office.

Thank you for your reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Delgado**
Member ID: W865123628
Date of birth: [Date of birth]
Date: [Date]

Enclosures: [List what you are sending — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-18; MRI report dated 2026-06-26; physical therapy discharge note; medication and injection records; surgeon's office notes]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```
